detailed_findings.finding: The telescoping identity and the algebraic combination of endpoint fractions are correct and yield the required witnesses A and B in Z[q].
The coprimality argument correctly uses that Z[q] is a UFD, hence irreducibles are prime and a common factor of M and B_0B_N must already divide B_0 or B_N.

reason: The proof matches the abstract telescoping lemma exactly. It correctly telescopes the finite sum to G_0-G_N, substitutes the endpoint representations, and explicitly constructs A=A_0B_N-A_NB_0 and B=B_0B_N in Z[q]. The coprimality claim gcd(B,M)=1 is then valid: any irreducible common divisor of M and B_0B_N would divide B_0 or B_N in the UFD Z[q], contradicting the endpoint coprimality assumptions. No material step is missing.
